sections.h2: Selling in the city of Frederick
sections.html:
Frederick is the seat of Frederick County, roughly 46 miles west of Baltimore and 50 miles north and slightly west of Washington, D.C. The city counted 78,171 people in 2020 and an estimated 92,059 by 2025.

Newer development surrounds a compact, walkable historic core, and that core is where most preservation rules apply. Interstates 70 and 270, U.S. 15 and U.S. 340 meet here, and MARC commuter rail and express bus 991 to the Shady Grove Metro station serve commuters, so buyers who work in the Washington area treat Frederick as a realistic home base. Fort Detrick is the largest employer in the area, with 10,827 jobs.

A house inside the city had a combined real property rate of 1.7382 per $100 of assessed value in the fiscal 2025 state table, built from a county piece and a city piece.

The city share funds street maintenance, trash removal and police. Homestead credit caps vary by municipality from 0 percent to 10 percent. A city address costs more per $100 than a county one, so buyers comparing Frederick with nearby areas will ask for the full bill. Keep a copy handy.

County Treasury sets September 30 as the due date for annual bills and first installments, and December 31 for second installments. Unpaid accounts pick up interest of 1 percent per month starting October 1. Payments in July earn a 1 percent discount, and August payments earn one-half percent.

You can reach Treasury at 30 North Market Street or 301-600-1111, weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. SDAT, which sets the assessed value, answers at 301-815-5350.

SDAT sets a new value about every third year. If yours looks off, appeal in this order:

  1. Supervisor of Assessments: 45 days from the notice date.
  2. Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board: 30 days after that decision.
  3. Maryland Tax Court: 30 days after the board's order.

The county also offers a Senior Tax Credit equal to 20 percent of net county real property taxes for owners 65 or older who meet income limits, and a Homestead Tax Credit that limits yearly increases in taxable value on a principal residence.

The Frederick Historic District holds more than 200 retailers, restaurants and antique shops along Market, Patrick and East Streets, and downtown has about 600 businesses and organizations. First Saturday draws about 11,000 people on average each month. West Patrick Street follows the old National Road, now U.S. 40, and Culler Lake is a man-made lake in the middle of town.

Daniel Dulany laid out the town by 1745, and Schifferstadt, built in 1756, is probably the oldest surviving house in the city. Older houses near the core often come with preservation review, mixed-age systems and surprises behind the walls. A seller who has permits, repair receipts and a recent inspection report on hand gives buyers fewer reasons to pause or ask for a lower price.

sections.h2: Historic district and exterior work rules
sections.html:
Exterior work on a designated site, or on a property in a Historic Preservation Overlay district, needs a certificate of approval from the Historic Preservation Commission. The commission reviews exterior features only, never interior layout. A home sale does not need its approval, but a buyer who plans a new porch, windows or siding will.

  • Changes need review even when they cannot be seen from the street. Routine maintenance and landscaping with no material effect are exempt.
  • The commission has 45 days to act on a complete application. If it does not act, the application is approved unless the applicant agrees to more time.
  • A certificate expires after three years without a building or zoning permit, with one six-month extension.
  • Anyone unhappy with a decision can go to the Circuit Court for Frederick County within 30 days.

Outside the overlay, a plan can still face demolition review when it removes more than 25 percent of floor area, changes significant roof lines or moves the structure. Tell your agent or buyer about any pending exterior plans early.

When you are selling, a short list helps. Gather the certificate of approval for any past exterior change, the building or zoning permit that went with it and any notice of violation that was closed. A house with gaps in that paper trail can lose a financed buyer late in the process, because the lender or the buyer's inspector will notice work that was never approved. If something is missing, ask the city's historic preservation staff how to resolve it before the house is listed rather than after a contract is signed.

Downtown has a flood history, and the Carroll Creek flood control project was built to reduce flood risk from the 100-year floodplain. A Carroll Creek Overlay District in the city code sets design standards for new construction and rehabilitation near the creek. If your house is close to the creek, expect a buyer to ask about the floodplain and the overlay standards, and have the answer ready from city planning.

Unpaid tax does not stop a sale, because the title company can pay it from your proceeds. The only real work is getting the figure right, and the earlier you start, the fewer surprises appear at the settlement table.

  1. Request a Lien Certificate or Tax Status Report from Treasury.
  2. Check for a separate city district tax or supplemental bill.
  3. Give the amounts to the title company before you set the closing date, since interest of 1 percent a month keeps adding to the balance.
  4. Pay the county and any city bill at closing from proceeds, then keep the receipts with your sale papers.

Rental condition for properties inside the city is handled by city inspectors at 301-600-3825, so a landlord selling should check for open complaints before listing. If the house needs work, a buyer paying cash can take it as-is, and the tax payoff is simply settled at the table.

faqs.q: What is the property tax rate in Frederick, MD?
faqs.a: The fiscal 2025 state table shows 1.7382 per $100 inside the city, made up of a 1.0077 county rate and a 0.7305 city rate. Rates reset yearly, so check your current notice.

faqs.q: When is Frederick property tax due?
faqs.a: September 30 for annual bills and the first installment, and December 31 for the second. Interest starts October 1 at 1 percent per month, and July payments get a 1 percent discount.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Frederick property tax?
faqs.a: Call the County Treasury at 301-600-1111 for billing, and SDAT at 301-815-5350 for the assessed value. Treasury is at 30 North Market Street.

faqs.q: Does the Historic Preservation Commission review a house sale?
faqs.a: No. Exterior work on a designated or overlay property needs approval, and the commission has 45 days to act on a complete application.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Frederick house with back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company pays the unpaid tax from your proceeds. Get a lien certificate or tax status report from Treasury so the amount is exact before you pick a closing date.
